Service Rules for Teaching and Non-teaching Employees of
the University, (First Amendment) 2021
In exercise of the powers conferred under section 35 and 38 of the U.P. Private Universities
Act 2019, the University brings the I st amendment in the Service Rules framed in 20 21,
namely:
1. Short Title, application and commencement:
1.1. These Rules may be called Teerthanker Mahaveer University Rules on Service
Conditions of the Teaching and Non -teaching Employees of the University
(First Amendment), 2021 and are framed in accordance with the provisions of
the section 38 of the U.P. Private Universities Act 2019.
1.2. These shall be effective on all the existing employees and also on employees
those who join the services of the University after the notifi cation of these
Rules.
The following amendments are being brought in the following clauses of the
Service Rules 2021.
2.8 Resignation, Termination and Retirement of the Teaching and Non-Teaching
employees:
i. If the University is willing to terminate the services of employee at the end of the
academic year two-months notice shall be given or one -month salary shall be
payable in lieu there-of as the case may be.
ii. Every permanent employee may resign his/her position after giving two months’
notice in writing to the University or three months’ salary in lieu of the notice in
the case of Teaching staff. However, the said Notice period for non-teaching staff
shall be one month. Every temporary employee may resign his/her post after
giving one-month notice in writing to the University or one-month salary in lieu of
the notice. The Executive Council is to accept the resignation and waiver of the
notice period. All permanent employees shall retire at the end of the month in
which they compl ete the age of superannuation i.e 58 years in case of class III
and IV non-teaching employees and 62 years in case of all teaching and class I &
II non-teaching employees of the University. Provided the Executive Council may
Teerthanker Mahaveer University
Rules of Service Conditions of the Teaching and Non-Teaching Employees of the University, 2021
permit the teaching staff to continue to serve after retirement as aforesaid till the
end of the academic year to ensure that the teaching work is not dislocated.
iii. Subject to the availability of the vacant positions and fitness, teachers as Assistant
Professor, Associate Professor and Professor/ Senior Professor/ Principal/
Director may be re -employed on contract appointment beyond the age of
superannuation, up to the age of 70 years.
2.7 Re-employment of retired persons:
The University may engage any person, who has superannuated, on contract to
serve the University in teaching and other academic activities or non -teaching
subject to such guidelines as the Executive Council may issue in this regard from
time to time, and pay shall be fixed according to qualification, experience in their
relevant field. The merit of the candidate shall be taken into account during this
appointment. The Executive Council is empowered to appoint any such person
with the recommendation of Selection Committee constituted in this reg ard
provided that no person who has attained the age of seventy years be appointed
under this option in case of teaching staff.

3. The record of all types of leave shall be maintained by the Payroll section of the University.

3.3 GENERAL RULES:
i. Leave cannot be claimed as matter of right. The sanctioning authority may refuse
or revoke leave of any kind.
ii. An employee on leave should not take up any service or employment elsewhere
during the leave.
iii. Minimum number for the medical leave to be taken at one time is 2 (two).
iv. An employee who is on leave for more than 04 (four) days on medical grounds will
be permitted to return to duty only on production of a medical certificate of fitness.
Leave sanctioning authority may secure second medical opinion if it is necessary.
v. The claim for compensatory leave shall be made with-in 90 days of such presence
on duty on weekly off/holiday.
vi. Compensatory leave once claimed and sanctioned, cannot be cancelled for any
reason.
vii. Absence from duty after the expiry of leave renders an employee liable for
disciplinary action.
viii. An employee who absents himself/herself without prior sanction of leave shall be
treated as absent and shall be subjected to disciplinary action.
ix. No employee shall leave the station without the prior permission of the designated
authority. He/she shall inform the authorities about his/her address during the days
of absence.
x. In case an employee leaving the country during the leave period, sanction of the
Vice Chancellor will be required, irrespective of the type or duration of leave.
xi. All types of leave shall remain suspended once/after an employee subm its his/her
resignation or gets such a notice from the college/ University.
xii. All leave shall be in reference to a calendar year, which stands for January 01st to
December 31st of that year.
3.4 EXPLANATORY NOTES:
i. CASUAL LEAVE:
a) An employee of the University shall be eligible for 12 (twelve) days casual leave in each
calendar year.
b) Casual leave cannot be carried forward to next year.
Teerthanker Mahaveer University
Rules of Service Conditions of the Teaching and Non-Teaching Employees of the University, 2021
c) In case of employee joining in middle of a year, the limit will proportionately be
reduced by the competent authority.
d) Casual leave is intended for a short time and cannot be granted more than 03 (three)
days at a time except under special circumstances.
e) Casual leave cannot be combined with any other type of leave, but can be prefixed or
suffixed with holidays and weekly-offs.
f) However, a non-teaching staff is allowed to take half -day casual leave only with the
permission of competent authority.
g) Application for CL must be made at least one day in advance and if not possible
under unforeseen circumst ances, then with -in three days of re -joining after the
leave.
ii. ACADEMIC/SPECIAL CASUAL LEAVE:
The Competent Authority may grant up to the limit of 10 (ten) days in a given calendar
year leave of absence from duty to a member of the teaching staff to perform such duties
as under:
a) To conduct examination of a University /Public Service Commission/board of
Examinations or any similar body/institution; and
b) To inspect academic institution attached to a statutory board/body.
Availing of such leave would be subject to the following conditions:
a) With prior approval from the competent authority on the recommendation of the
college Director/Principal.
b) Submission of a copy of invitation letter from the host organization.
Regarding AL(s) if any faculty, who leaves the job within the period of one year, will
be liable to repay the salary of the days for which he/she has availed the AL(s) during
the first year of his/her service.
iii. MEDICAL LEAVE:
a) Regular employees except class IV and Hostel staff of the Univers ity shall be
eligible for 08 (eight) days medical leave in a calendar year to meet out the
requirement rising due to illness.
b) For availing four or more medical leave, submission of medical certificate from
registered medical practitioner is a must.
c) Medical leave cannot be prefixed or suffixed with holidays and weekly -offs.
Medical leave can be carried forward and accumulated to the extent of 30 (thirty)
days and cannot be encashed. More than 30 ML(s) will lapse automatically on 31st
December of the year.
Teerthanker Mahaveer University
Rules of Service Conditions of the Teaching and Non-Teaching Employees of the University, 2021
iv. EARNED LEAVE:
a) Non vacation staff (staff that is not entitled for summer/winter vacation) shall be
entitled for 10 (ten) days earned leave, which are admissible after 01 (one) year of
regular service.
b) Earned leave can be accumulated up to 60 (sixty) days. The maximum number of
earned leave that can be granted in a calendar year is 60 (sixty) days only.
c) Encashment of earned leave will be either on retirement or on resignation after
02 (two) years of minimum service.
d) Normally earned leave can be availed for a minimum 03 (three) days at a time.
e) Sundays/holidays occurring during the period of EL will be counted into/treated
as part of leave applied for.
f) In case an employee clubs EL with CL on Monday, then the non -working day,
Sunday shall also be treated as EL.
v. VACATION LEAVE:
Faculty shall avail vacation leave in two spells i.e. summer and winter. Normally the
duration of summer and winter vacation shall be as under:
 Winter Vacation: 07 (Seven) days
 Summer Vacation: 14 (Fourteen) days
a) The dates of commencement and duration of leave may be decided as per the
requirement of the college with prior intimation to the Vice Chancellor.
b) Teachers shall be given credit of leave in earned leave account for the vacation
period in the ratio of 1:1, if detailed for official work by the competent authority
during vacation. Such converted leave into earned leave account shall be governed
by the earned leave rules for the non vacation staff as stated above. For the faculty
whose services are requisitioned during the vacation, the Principal/Director/HOD
concerned shall seek the prior permission of the Vice Chancellor.
c) Faculty on completion of 01 (one) year of service in the University shall become
eligible to avail vacation leave.
d) Directors/Principals of an academic unit (College/Department/Centre) would be
entitled for 21 (Twenty One) days of earned leave in lieu of vacation leave and shall
not be carried forward.
e) Vacation leaves or Earned Leaves converted in lieu of Vacation Leaves to
Teaching Staff cannot be carried forwarded to the next calendar year.
vi. COMPENSATORY LEAVE:
a) Non-teaching staff called to perform official duty on weekly-offs or public holidays
shall be granted compensatory leave of equal number of days.
Teerthanker Mahaveer University
Rules of Service Conditions of the Teaching and Non-Teaching Employees of the University, 2021
b) However, if employee is called to clear the arrear of work for which he or she is
personally responsible or is imposed as a penalty, no compensatory leave shall be
granted under such situations.
c) No compensatory leave shall be admissible to an employee who is paid TA & DA
for that day(s).
d) Such compensatory leave may be availed within 03 (three) month s of the
entitlement otherwise same shall be treated as lapsed.
vii. EXTRA-ORDINARY LEAVE:
In case of genuine necessity and when no other leave is due, leave without pay may be
granted subject to the conditions to be specified at the time of granting the leave.
viii. STUDY LEAVE:
a) A faculty member after completing five years of service with the University may
be granted study leave with half pay and on execution of a bond to serve the
University for another 05 (five) years after availing such leave failing which he or
she would be asked to deposit an amount equivalent full salary of the period for
which study leave have been availed.
b) Study leave can be granted to a faculty for a maximum period of 24 (twenty four )
months in entire career with University. However, in exceptional cases it could be
further extended to another 12 (twelve) months to the satisfaction of the
Competent Authority.
c) Study leave shall be granted for acquiring higher qualification, if the add itional
qualification is considered to be in the interest of the college/ University.
ix. MATERNITY LEAVE:
a) Female employees after 02 (two) years of their service with the University may be
granted 90 (ninety) days of maternity leave with half pay.
b) This is admissible to employees up to the second child.
c) The leave can be combined with any other kind of leave.
d) Maternity leave shall be granted only if supported by a medical certificate.
e) Employees covered under ESIC would either the benefits of the ESIC scheme o r the
Maternity Leave of the University.
x. HOSPITALIZATION LEAVE:
Hospital leave may be granted to an employee under medical treatment for illness or
injury directly due to risk incurred in the course of his official duty. This concession will be
available to such employee, the nature of whose duties exposes them to such illness or
injury. Hospitalization leave may be granted up to a period of 03 (three) months on full or
Teerthanker Mahaveer University
Rules of Service Conditions of the Teaching and Non-Teaching Employees of the University, 2021
half salary, as may be decided by the competent authority, in any period of 0 3 (three)
years.
4. Code of Conduct for Employees:
a. These code of Conduct Rules shall apply to every person appointed by the
University including the Part-Time, Contract, Adhoc and temporary appointees
b. Every employee shall confirm to and abide by the rule s including the
employees Code of Conduct Rules and shall observe, comply with obey all
orders and directions which may from time to time be given to him/her by any
person under whose jurisdiction, superintendence or control he/she may be
placed. Ignorance of the rules cannot be an excuse.
c. Every employee shall serve the University honestly and faithfully and shall use
his/her utmost endeavors to promote the interests of the University and shall
show courtesy and attention in all transactions and interactio ns with every
person with whom he/she may be in contact in his/her capacity as an
employee whether uniformed or not, shall dress properly, neatly and presently
always and every employee present a cheerful and dignified appearance.
Employees shall spend the ir time on work and shall avoid wasting time on
gossiping/ purposeless talk. They should go about as silently as possible with
their duties. Executive Council may prescribe other rules time to time observe
decorum and discipline.
d. Every employee of the University shall be required:
i. To maintain absolute integrity
ii. To maintain devotion to duty
iii. To confirm and abide by the Rules and Regulations of the University.
iv. To abide by lawful orders and direction in the course of official duties
by any person or persons to whom he/she is sub-ordinate in the service
of the University, he/she shall not involve anti -social activity or create
any communal disharmony.
e. No employee should use his/her position or influence directly or indirectly to
secure and benefits.
f. No employee shall take part in election except prior written permission from
the Executive Council.
g. No employee can join any association, the object or activities wh ich are
prejudicial to the interest and sovereignty and integrity of India or to the
interest of the University or public order.
h. No employee shall participate in any demonstration which is prejudicial to the
interest of the sovereignty and integrity of In dia, security of the State, the
interest of the University, public order or morality or which involves contempt
of court and defamation including inciting the students against other students
or employees of the University or administration or in any way ab et or any
Teerthanker Mahaveer University
Rules of Service Conditions of the Teaching and Non-Teaching Employees of the University, 2021
form of strike or coercion or physical duress in connection with any matter
pertaining to his/her service or the service of any other employee or any other
employees of the University
i. No employee shall except previous sanction of the University, ask for or accept
contribution or otherwise associate himself/herself to receive any funds or
other collection in cash/ cheque or any kind.
j. No employee shall except previous sanction of the University engage directly
or indirectly in any trade or business or to undertake any other employment.
k. No employee shall bring or attempt to bring any political, personal or other
influences to bear upon any authority of the University to further his/her
interest or interest of any other person in respect of matters pertaining to
his/her service or in respect of any other matter involving pecuniary or other
benefits to him/her.
l. No employee shall involve intoxicating drinks or possess any of them in the
University premises.
m. An employee shall not make representations to the Executive
Council/Academic Council or Government or to any authority of the University
directly and such representations shall be made through the proper channel.
n. An employee of the University except in accordance with any general or special
order of the Executive Council or in the performance in good faith of the duties
assigned to him/her, shall not communicate directly or indirectly any official
documents or information to any employee or to any other person to whom
he/she is not authorized to communicate such documents or information.
o. Concerted or organized refusal on the part of the employee to receive their
pay shall constitute misconduct.
p. An employee of the University may be placed under suspension where an
enquiry in to charges is pending or contemplated against him/her.
q. An employee of the University who is placed under suspension shall be paid
subsistence allowance during the period of suspension, not exceeding one half
of the basic pay and such proportions of the allowances as the Executive
Council may determine.
r. No employee shall avail any kind of leave without prior approval of the
competent authority or extend the period of leave sanctioned without the
approval of the competent authority as mentioned in the leave rules above. If
an employee remains absent from his/her duties for a period exceeding 10
days without any prior approval or intimation, it shall be taken for granted that
the said employee is no more interested in serving the University and shall be
deemed to have left the services of the University on his/her own accord and
there shall be no claim on the University from such employee. The University
shall issue the notice in this regard to the employee and no claim on University
by such employee shall be his/her right or legitimate.
Teerthanker Mahaveer University

TMU Regulations on Minimum Qualifications for Appointment
of Teachers and other Academic Staff in the University, 2021
(Approved by the Executive Council in its 19th meeting dated 12.06.2021)
TEERTHANKER MAHAVEER UNIVERSITY
MORADABAD
Regulations on Minimum Qualifications for Appointment of Teachers and other Academic Staff, 2021
Teerthanker Mahaveer University, Moradabad
TEERTHANKER MAHAVEER UNIVERSITY
MORADABAD – 244001 (U.P.)
TMU REGULATIONS ON MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS FOR
APPOINTMENT OF TEACHERS AND OTHER ACADEMIC STAFF IN THE
UNIVERSITY, 2021.
In exercise of the powers conferred under section 3 5 of the U.P. Private Universities Act 2019 and in
suppression of the Recruitment Policy, 2013 together with all amendments (if any) made there -in from
time to time, the University frames the following Regulations, namely:
1. Short Title, application and commencement:
1.1. These Regulations may be called Teerthanker Mahaveer University Regulations on
Minimum Qualifications for Appointment of Teachers and other Academic Staff in the
University, 2021 and are framed in accordance with the UGC Regulations on Minimum
Qualifications for appointment of teachers and other academic staff in Universities and
Colleges and other Measures for Maintenance of Standards of Higher Education), 2018
notified vide Gazette Notification No. F.1-2/2017(EC/PS) dated 18 July 2018 and other
Regulations on minimum qualifications for appointment of teachers and other academic
staff by the concerned regulatory/statutory bodies like MCI, DCI, PCI, BCI, NCTE,
AICTE and ICAR etc.
1.2. These sha ll apply for appointment of teaching and other academic staff in all the
departments/ colleges of the University.
1.3. These shall be effective from the date of its approval by the Executive Council.
1.4. The service conditions of the University Teachers, Librarians and Directors of Physical
Education and Sports shall be provided by these Regulations.
1.5. After the commencement of these Regulations a ny appointment made there-after in
contraventions to the provisions of these Regulations shall stand null and void.
Regulations on Minimum Qualifications for Appointment of Teachers and other Academic Staff, 2021
Teerthanker Mahaveer University, Moradabad
2. General Principles for Recruitment and Qualifications and Age of Superannuation:
2.1 The direct recruitment to the posts of Assistant Professor, Associate Professor, Professor
and Sen ior Professor in the University shall be on basis of merit through an
advertisement, followed by the duly constituted Selection Committee as per the
provisions made under these Regulations.
2.2 The minimum qualifications for appointment to the post of Assistant Professor, Associate
Professor, Professor, Senior Professor, Principal, Librarian, Deputy Librarian, Assistant/
Librarian, Director- Physical Education, Deputy Director- Physical Education, Assistant
Director- Physical Education shall be as specified in these Regulations.
2.3 (a) The National Eligibility Test (NET) or an accredited State Level Eligibility Test
(SLET/SET) shall be the minimum eligibility for appointment to the post of Assistant
Professor.
(b) I n the disciplines of Medical, Dental, Nursing, Para -medical, Physiotherapy,
Engineering, Computer Applications, Pharmacy and Management , for the appointment
to the post of Assistant Professor, the post-graduation degree with first class or equivalent
and relevant experience (if any) as specified in these Regulations, shall be the minimum
eligibility.
Provided, the candidates who have acquired Ph.D. degree in accordance with the UGC
Regulations governing the Minimum Standards and Procedure for the Award of M.Phil./
Ph.D. Degree, 2009 or 2016 and their subsequent amendments from time to time, shall
be exempted from the requirement of NET/SLET/SET for recruitment and appointment
of Assistant Professor in the University or equivalent positions in University subject to
the fulfillment of the following conditions:
a) The Ph.D. degree of the candidate has been awarded in regular mode only;
b) The Ph.D. thesis has been awarded by at least two external examiners;
c) An open Ph.D. viva voce of the candidate has been conducted;
d) The candidate has published two research papers from his/ her Ph.D. work out of which
at least one is in a refereed journal;
e) The candidate has presented at least two papers, based on his/ her Ph.D. work in
conferences/seminars sponsored/funded/supported by the UGC/ ICSSR/CSIR or any
similar agency.
The fulfilment of these conditions is to be certified by the Registrar or the Dean
(Academic Affairs) of the University concerned.
Regulations on Minimum Qualifications for Appointment of Teachers and other Academic Staff, 2021
Teerthanker Mahaveer University, Moradabad
2.4 The clearing of NET/SLET/SET shall not be required for candidates in such disciplines
for which NET/SLET/SET has not been conducted.
2.5 The Ph.D. Degree shall be a mandatory qualification for appointment and promotion to
the post of Associate Professor and Professor.
2.6 The Ph.D. Degree shall be a mandatory qualification for promotion to the post of
Assistant Professor (Selection Grade/Academic Level 12).
2.7 The Ph.D. Degree shall be a mandatory qualification for the direct recruitment to the post
of Assistant Professor in disciplines other than mentioned in sub -clause 2.3 (b) above,
with effect from 01.07.2021.
2.8 The time taken by candidates to acquire Ph.D. degree shall not be considered as
teaching/ research experience to be claimed for appointment to the teaching positions.
Further, the period of active service spent on pursuing Ph.D. degree simultaneously with
teaching assignment without taking any kind of leave , shall be counted as teaching
experience for the purpose of direct recruitment/ promotion.
2.9 Age of Superannuation & Extension post superannuation: The age of superannuation
for all faculty members and Principals/ Directors of institutions/ colleges/ schools shall
be 65 years. Subject to the availability of the vacant positions and fitness, teachers as
Assistant Professor, Associate Professor and Professor/ Senior Professor/ Principal/
Director may be re-employed on contract appointment beyond the age of superannuation,
up to the age of 70 years.
3. Constitution of Selection Committee and Guidelines on Selection Procedures:
The Selection Committee shall comprises of the following:
a) The Selection Committee for the post of Assistant Professor, Associate Professor,
Professor and Senior Professor in the University shall have the following
composition:

viii) Registrar Member Secretary

b) Four members, including two outside subject experts, shall constitute the quorum.
c) Selection Committees for the posts of Directors, Deputy Directors, Assistant Directors of
Physical Education, Librarians, Deputy Librarians and Assistant Librarians shall be the
same as that of Professor, Associate Professor and Assistant Professor respectively.
4. Direct Recruitment/ Promotion of Incumbent:
a) Counting of Past service for Direct Recruitment and Promotion for the posts as mentioned in
sub-clause 3(a) as above:
b) Previous regular service, whether national or international, as Assistant Professor, Associate
Professor or Professor or equivalent in University, College, National Laboratories or other
scientific/ professional organizations such as CSIR, ICAR, DRDO, UGC, ICSSR, ICHR,
ICMR, DBT or State PSUs etc., s hall be taken into account for direct recruitment as an
Assistant Professor, Associate Professor or Professor, provided that:
i) The qualifications for the post held are not lower than the qualifications as
mentioned above in sub-clause 3.1.
ii) The post is/ was in an equivalent grade Assistant Professor, Associate Professor
or Professor.
iii) The concerned Assistant Professor, Associate Professor or Professor should
possess the same qualifications as prescribed above in sub-clause 3.1 for the posts
of Assistant Professor, Associate Professor or Professor, as the case may be.
iv) The previous appointment was not as Guest Faculty for any duration or ad-hoc or
in a leave vacancy of less than one year duration. Ad-hoc or temporary service of
more than one year duration can be counted.
c) Equivalence of Experience of Diploma level Institutions and Degree level Institutions:
Experience at Diploma level Polytechnic shall be considered equivalent to the Degree
level institution at appropriate level, as applicable provided, qualifications,
experience and research contribution are same for the post under consideration as per
the present Regulations.
d) Cadre Structure:
a. Minimum 1:2:6 of cadre ratio to be maintained for Professor: Associate
Professor: Assistant Professor respectively.
b. Principal/ Director shall be outside the purview of cadre ratio.
e) Eligibility of direct Ph.D. after B.E./ B.Tech.
The qua lification of Ph.D . acquired directly after B.E./ B.Tech. is applicable in
Technical departments/ colleges of the University, provided degree of Ph.D. awarded
is in relevant discipline by recognized University following UGC Ph.D. Regulations
as the time bei ng in force or has been awarded by the Institutions of national

Teerthanker Mahaveer University, Moradabad
importance like IITs, IIMs, NITs etc. duly recognized by MHRD. Further, the
candidate should have obtained B.E./B.Tech. Degree in first class.
5. Qualifications:
No person shall be appointed to the post of Assistant Professor, Associate Professor,
Professor and Senior Professor , Librarian or Director of Physical Education, in the
university if such person does not fulfil the requirements as to the qualifications fo r the
appropriate post as provided in the Regulations.

5.4.1 Eligibility for Post-graduate teachers: Only those teachers who possess at least five
years teaching experience obtained in approved/ recognized Pharmacy College after
passing M.Pharm/ Pharm.D course or three years teaching experience after Ph.D. shall
be recognized by the PCI as post –graduate pharmacy teachers.
5.4.2 The candidature of the holders of equivalent qualifications as approved by the
Pharmacy council of India form time to time shall also be considered for the
appointment.
5.4.3 The candidature of the holders of equivalent qualifications as approved by the
Pharmacy council of India form time to time shall also be considered for the
appointment.
5.4.4 A Pharmacy teacher shall be considered as the teacher in the Pharmacy College of the
University in an academic year (1st July to 30th June of next calendar year). In case
the person was already considered teacher during particular academic year in any other
Pharmacy College, he/she shall not be eligible for appointment as teacher in the
University in same academic year.

TMU Regulations Governing Admissions to various programmes
of the University (Except Medical and Dental), 2026
(To be Approved by the Executive Council during its next meeting)
TEERTHANKER MAHAVEER UNIVERSITY
MORADABAD
Page 1 of 7
TEERTHANKER MAHAVEER UNIVERSITY
MORADABAD – 244001 (U.P.)
TMU REGULATIONS GOVERNING ADMISSIONS TO VARIOUS PROGRAMMES OF THE UNIVERSITY
(EXCEPT MEDICAL AND DENTAL), 2026-27
In exercise of the powers conferred under section 30 of the Teethanker Mahaveer University,
Uttar Pradesh Act, 2008 and in suppression of Regulations, 2008 together with all
amendments (if any) made there-in from time to time, the University frames the following
Regulations, namely:
1. Short Title, application and commencement:
1.1 These Regulations may be called Teerthanker Mahaveer University Regulations
governing admission to various programmes of the University (except Medical and
Dental).
1.2 These shall apply to candidates/students seeking admissions in programmes of
study offered in various the departments/colleges of the University.
1.3 The terms and conditions related to admission and cancellation of admissions shall
be provided by these Regulations.
2. Objectives:
To promote excellence in procedures and have transparency in the various
processes related with admissions, the University has framed these regulations.
3. Admission to the programme of Study in the University:
3.01 As per the provisions of the section 12 of the Act and clause 1.06 of the Statutes of
the Teerthanker Mahaveer University, there shall be an Admission Committee. The
composition of the Admission Committee shall be as:
i) Vice Chancellor Chairperson

Policy for Formulation and Review of Vision, Mission of the
University/College/Department/Centre and PEOs, PSOs, POs &
COs of the Programme
1. Purpose of the Policy
This policy establishes a structured, transparent, and outcome-driven framework for the
development, approval, alignment, dissemination, assessment and periodic review of Vision,
Mission of the University/College/Department/Centre and PEOs, PSOs, POs & COs across all
programmes of the University.
2. Scope of the Policy:
This policy applies to Faculties, Colleges, Departments, Centres and Undergraduate,
Postgraduate, and Doctoral Programmes and all teaching and academic support units of
Teerthanker Mahaveer University.
3. Definitions
3.1 Vision
A vision is an outline of all the future goals of the Institution. It gives a brief overview on long-
term objectives of Institutions. Vision statement can be viewed as a guide for choosing actions
that support the goals of the organisation.
An effective vision statement helps an organisation in:
(a) Motivate people and maintain their focus within the organisation.
(b) Make quicker and more informed judgements.
(c) Attract talented individuals.
3.2 Mission
A mission is the measures taken by an Institution to achieve its vision. It gives an Institution's
actions a distinct dimension. It establishes the purpose of the organisation and keep the focus
in the right direction.
A mission statement should clearly state the following:
a) What organisation does?
Page 2 of 12
b) The manner in which the organisation operates.
c) Rationale behind organization's actions.
d) A mission statement shall be simple, straightforward, and operative and be known to every
member of the organisation.
3.3 Programme Educational Objectives (PEOs)
PEOs are broad statements that describe the expected achievement of graduates that the
program is preparing graduates to achieve. PEOs state that graduates could demonstrate certain
skillsets within a period of 3 to 5 years after graduation.
The following details need to be considered while defining the program's educational
objectives:
 PEOs should align with the Institution's mission.
 Institution's faculty and stakeholders should actively participate in framing the PEOs.
 PEOs needs to be precise.
 PEO shall be manageable and achievable by the program.
3.4 Programme Outcomes (POs)
POs are statements that describe what students are expected to know and be able to do upon
graduating from the Program. These are related to description of the knowledge, skills,
attitudes, competences, and values a student display at the completion of the program.
 POs shall be specific, measurable and achievable
 POs shall be in line with the graduate attributes
3.5 Programme Specific Outcomes (PSOs)
PSOs are a statement that describes what students are expected to know and be able to do in a
specialised area of discipline upon graduating from a program. These are defined for a program,
if required.
3.6 Course Outcomes (COs)
COs are narrower statements that describe what students are expected to learn at completion of
a course. These outcomes should be meaningful, observable and measurable. These outcomes
are mainly affective, cognitive and behavioural outcomes.
 COs shall derive from the program outcome.
 Shall begin with the action verb from Bloom’s taxonomy
4. Policy Principles
1. Alignment with national regulatory bodies (NBA, NAAC, UGC, PCI, AICTE, BCI,
etc.)
2. Outcome-Based Education (OBE) orientation
Page 3 of 12
3. Stakeholders’ participation
4. Transparency and documentation
5. Continuous Quality Improvement Cycle (CQI)
6. Periodic Review and Revision

The Academic Council initiates the process of framing the Vision and Mission of the
University. It also undertakes periodic review and updating of the Vision and Mission to ensure
continued relevance, alignment with institutional goals, and changing academic/regulatory
requirements.

5.3 POs and PSOs Formulation: Developed in alignment with NBA Graduate Attributes and
in compliance with guidelines prescribed by the relevant regulatory and statutory bodies ,
ensuring outcome-based education, quality standards, and academic relevance . While writing
POs and PSOs the following questions/points must be addressed properly:
Page 5 of 12
 The quality of a programme is ultimately assessed by the ability of the learner to carry
out their expected roles and responsibilities in society. This requires the programme to
have a clear statement of its outcomes.
 The specific competencies that the students should demonstrate at the end of the
programme should be clearly defined.
 The programme must demonstrate how the component modules/chapters contribute to
the fulfilment of the programme’s outcomes.
 The programme must show how the student is able to demonstrate the learning
outcomes, for example, through assessments.
 The link between competencies expected at the end of the programme and those
expected during training and the workplace (such as entrepreneurship) should be clearly
specified.

5.4 COs Formulation: Prepared by course teachers (subject matter expert) using Bloom’s
Taxonomy action verbs and Mapping with POs & PSOs. While writing COs the following
questions/points must be addressed properly:
Specific: Are there a description of precise behaviour and the situation it will be performed in?
Is it concrete, detailed, focused and defined?
Measurable: Can the performance of the outcome be observed and measured?
Achievable: With a reasonable number of efforts and application can the outcome be achieved?
Are you attempting too much?
Page 6 of 12
Relevant: Is the outcome important or worthwhile to the learner or stakeholder? Is it possible
to achieve this outcome?
Time-Bound: Is there a time limit, rate number, percentage or frequency clearly stated? When
will this outcome be accomplished?
 COs shall be written by the course teacher (subject expert).
 Course outcomes shall contain an action verb from Bloom's taxonomy.

Faculty Development Policy
1. Policy Preamble
Teerthanker Mahaveer University is committed to promoting continuous professional
development of its faculty members to ensure excellence in teaching, research, innovation, and
academic leadership. The University recognizes that faculty competence and professional
growth are essential for sustaining academic quality and responding effectively to evolving
educational, technological, and societal needs.
2. Purpose of the Policy
This policy aims to:
 Promote structured and continuous professional development of faculty.
 Enhance teaching-learning methodologies and pedagogical practices.
 Strengthen research, innovation, and academic leadership.
 Encourage national and international academic engagement.
 Support lifelong learning and professional advancement.
3. Scope and Applicability
This policy applies to:
 All teaching faculty members (full-time, part-time, contractual).
4. Internal Faculty Development Initiatives
The University shall organize and facilitate structured development initiatives including:
 Faculty Development Programmes (FDPs)
 Workshops and Seminars on teaching-learning processes
 Training programmes on innovative pedagogical methods
 Sessions on academic quality assurance processes
Page 2 of 4
 Programmes on communication skills, emotional intelligence, and professional
competencies
 Orientation and refresher programmes aligned with evolving academic frameworks
These initiatives are aimed at strengthening academic delivery and professional growth.
5. External Academic Engagement and Professional Promotion
Recognizing the importance of broader academic exposure, the University shall encourage and
support faculty participation in external academic and professional development activities,
including:
5.1 Conferences, Seminars & FDPs
 Presentation of research papers at National and International Conferences/Seminars.
 Participation in Seminars, Symposiums, and Academic Conclaves.
 Engagement in interdisciplinary academic discussions and forums.
 Participation in Entrepreneurship/Incubation/Innovation activities
 Participation in FDPs and Case Development Workshops
5.2 Research and Scholarly Activities
 Participation in research methodology workshops.
 Submission of research proposals to funding agencies.
 Publication of research articles in peer-reviewed journals.
 Contribution to edited books, book chapters, and academic publications.
 Collaboration with other institutions for joint research initiatives.
 University funded projects (Seed Money) and externally funded projects
5.3 Training and Certification Programmes
 Enrolment in subject-specific refresher courses.
 Participation in online and blended learning programmes.
 Completion of certified training programmes relevant to discipline or pedagogy.
 Engagement in professional certification programmes that enhance subject expertise.
5.4 Academic Networking and Collaboration
 Academic exchange programmes and collaborative interactions.
 Industry-academia interface programmes.
 Participation in professional bodies and academic associations.
Page 3 of 4
 Engagement in expert lectures, invited talks, and knowledge-sharing platforms.
5.5 Community and Extension Engagement
 Participation in outreach and extension programmes.
 Involvement in capacity-building workshops for external stakeholders.
 Academic consultancy and advisory engagements, as permitted by institutional norms.
6. Institutional Support and Facilitation
The University shall:
 Facilitate participation of faculty in various capacity building programmes.
 Encourage documentation of professional development activities.
 Recognize faculty achievements in research and academic contributions.
 Promote dissemination of acquired knowledge within the institution.
 Support for the Academic Leave as per University Leave Policy.
 Support financially under Financial Incentive and Financial Assistance Scheme of the
University
 Handhold faculty in executing various funded projects.
7. Monitoring and Documentation
 Records of faculty development activities shall be maintained at the institutional level.
 Participation, outcomes, and academic contributions shall be documented.
 Periodic review may be undertaken to assess effectiveness and alignment with
institutional goals.
8. Development of detailed Policies /SOPs to support this Policy
The University has formulated and implemented various Policies and Standard
Operating Procedures (SOPs) to support and promote the professional development of
its faculty members. These policies are uniformly applicable to all full-time faculty
members of TMU and are designed to encourage academic excellence, research
advancement, consultancy engagement, and overall professional growth and mentioned
below:
 TMU Regulation on Financial Assistance to Faculty for Promotion of Research and
Students Participation in Extracurricular Activities-2021.
 Policy on Consultancy & Research Projects.
 TMU Seed Money Grant Scheme-2021.

Waste Management Policy
1. Policy Overview
Teerthanker Mahaveer University is committed to maintaining a clean, sustainable, and
environmentally responsible campus through responsible waste management practices. The
University recognizes that waste management is an important institutional responsibility that
contributes to environmental sustainability and campus hygiene.
The University promotes environmentally responsible behaviour among students, faculty, staff,
and visitors by encouraging responsible waste disposal practices and supporting broader
environmental initiatives implemented across the campus.
2. Policy Statement
Teerthanker Mahaveer University strives to create a clean and sustainable campus environment
by implementing appropriate waste management practices in accordance with institutional
sustainability initiatives and applicable environmental regulations.
The University recognizes waste management as an institutional, environmental, and social
responsibility, and encourages active participation of the university community in maintaining
a clean and environmentally responsible campus.
3. Objectives of the Policy
The objectives of this policy are to:
1. Promote responsible waste management practices across the University campus.
2. Encourage waste segregation and proper disposal practices.
3. Reduce waste generation through awareness and sustainable consumption practices.
4. Promote environmentally responsible behaviour among students, faculty, and staff.
5. Support campus cleanliness and environmental sustainability initiatives.
6. Contribute to broader sustainability efforts promoted through institutional activities.
Page 2 of 8
4. Scope of the Policy
This policy applies to all areas within the University campus, including:
 Academic buildings and classrooms
 Administrative offices
 Laboratories and research facilities
 Library and learning spaces
 Hostels and dining facilities
 Hospital and clinical facilities associated with the University
 Sports and recreational areas
 Common campus areas and public spaces
The policy applies to all members of the University community including students, faculty
members, administrative staff, service providers, and visitors.
5. Waste Classification
Effective waste management requires proper identification and categorization of different types
of waste generated across the University campus. Teerthanker Mahaveer University recognizes
that waste generated within an academic institution arises from diverse activities including
teaching, research, residential facilities, healthcare services, administrative operations, Mess,
Cafeterias and campus maintenance. For the purpose of responsible management and disposal,
waste generated within the campus may broadly be classified into the following categories.
5.1 Biodegradable Waste
Biodegradable waste refers to organic materials that can naturally decompose through
biological processes. This type of waste is commonly generated from food preparation,
landscaping activities etc. and typical examples include:
 Food waste generated from hostels, cafeterias, and dining facilities
 Garden and horticultural waste such as leaves, grass clippings, and plant residues
 Paper napkins and other biodegradable organic materials
Proper handling and environmentally responsible disposal of biodegradable waste help
maintain campus hygiene and reduce environmental impact.
Page 3 of 8
5.2 Dry Recyclable Waste
Dry recyclable waste consists of materials that can potentially be reused or recycled through
appropriate waste processing mechanisms. These materials are typically non-biodegradable but
recyclable when collected and managed properly.
Examples include:
 Paper and cardboard materials generated from academic and administrative activities
 Plastic containers, bottles, and packaging materials
 Metal cans and aluminium containers
 Packaging materials used in laboratories or offices
Encouraging responsible disposal and segregation of recyclable materials helps support
sustainable resource management and reduces unnecessary accumulation of waste.
5.3 Sanitary and Hygiene Waste
Sanitary waste refers to waste generated from personal hygiene and sanitation activities across
the campus. Such waste requires careful handling to ensure hygienic conditions and prevent
contamination.
Examples include:
 Sanitary napkins and personal hygiene products
 Tissues and other hygiene-related disposable materials
Appropriate disposal mechanisms are encouraged to maintain cleanliness and sanitation
standards across campus facilities such as hostels, restrooms, and common areas.
5.4 Electronic Waste (E-Waste)
Electronic waste refers to discarded electrical and electronic equipment that is no longer
functional or has reached the end of its useful life. As a modern academic institution with
significant use of digital infrastructure, the University may generate electronic waste through
its academic, administrative, and technological activities.
Examples include:
 Computers and laptops
Page 4 of 8
 Printers and scanners
 Electronic peripherals and communication devices
 Obsolete electronic components or equipment
Electronic waste must be handled carefully due to the presence of electronic components and
materials that require appropriate disposal in accordance with environmental guidelines.
5.5 Non-Recyclable Waste
Non-recyclable waste includes materials that cannot be easily reused or recycled through
conventional processes. These materials require proper disposal through designated waste
handling systems. Responsible disposal practices help ensure that such waste does not
adversely affect the campus environment.
Examples include:
 Mixed waste materials that cannot be segregated for recycling
 Certain packaging materials
 Contaminated disposable items
5.6 Biomedical Waste
Biomedical waste refers to waste generated during medical, laboratory, diagnostic, or research
activities that may pose potential risks to human health and the environment. Such waste
requires careful handling, segregation, treatment, and disposal in accordance with prescribed
regulatory guidelines. Adherence to proper biomedical waste management practices is essential
to prevent contamination, infection, and environmental hazards.
Examples include:
 Used personal protective equipment (PPE) such as gloves, masks, and gowns
 Laboratory waste including cultures, specimens, and contaminated materials
 Sharps such as needles, syringes, and blades
 Discarded medicines and pharmaceutical waste
6. Waste Segregation Practices
Effective waste management within the University campus begins with segregation of waste at
the point of generation. Teerthanker Mahaveer University encourages the practice of separating
Page 5 of 8
different types of waste at the source in order to ensure proper handling, reduce environmental
impact, and facilitate responsible disposal and recycling practices. Waste segregation helps
prevent the mixing of biodegradable, recyclable, sanitary, and non-recyclable waste streams,
thereby improving the efficiency of waste management processes and maintaining hygienic
conditions across the campus.
6.1 Source-Level Segregation
All members of the University community, including students, faculty, administrative staff,
service personnel, and visitors, are encouraged to dispose of waste responsibly by segregating
it at the point of generation. This practice supports environmentally responsible waste handling
and promotes a culture of sustainability within the University.
Segregation at the source ensures that:
 Biodegradable waste can be handled separately from recyclable materials.
 Recyclable waste can be recovered and processed appropriately.
 Sanitary and non-recyclable waste is disposed of safely and hygienically.
6.2 Waste Segregation Infrastructure
To facilitate proper waste segregation, appropriate waste disposal infrastructure is provided
across the University campus. Waste bins and collection points are placed at strategic locations
to enable convenient and responsible disposal of waste by members of the campus community.
Waste collection facilities are typically available in areas such as:
 Academic buildings and classrooms
 Administrative offices
 Libraries and study areas
 Laboratories and research facilities
 Hostels and dining areas
 Common areas and corridors
 Sports and recreational facilities
 Parking areas and open spaces
 Food lane (V arious food outlets area)
These facilities support the maintenance of campus cleanliness and help ensure effective waste
collection practices.
Page 6 of 8
6.3 Use of Designated Waste Bins
Wherever feasible, designated waste bins may be used to encourage the segregation of different
types of waste. These bins help individuals identify appropriate disposal methods and prevent
the mixing of waste categories.
Typical waste segregation practices may include the use of bins for:
Waste Category Description

residues

6.4 Cleanliness and Hygiene Practices
Regular collection and removal of waste from designated disposal points is necessary to
maintain hygienic campus conditions. Proper waste handling practices help prevent
accumulation of waste and ensure a clean and healthy environment for students, staff, and
visitors.
Members of the University community are encouraged to:
 Dispose of waste only in designated bins.
 Avoid littering within the campus premises.
 Follow institutional guidelines related to environmental cleanliness.
Maintaining cleanliness within classrooms, hostels, offices, and common areas is considered a
shared responsibility of all campus stakeholders.
Page 7 of 8

The success of waste segregation practices depends on the active participation of the University

Awareness activities, environmental campaigns, and cleanliness drives organized within the
campus help reinforce the importance of waste segregation and responsible environmental
behaviour. Through collective participation, the University aims to promote a culture of
environmental responsibility and maintain a clean and sustainable campus environment.
7. Waste Reduction Initiatives
The University promotes waste reduction through various sustainable practices, including:
7.1 Paper Reduction
 Adoption of digital communication systems
 Online submission of academic documents

7.2 Plastic Reduction
The University discourages the use of single-use plastics within the campus, and awareness

students and staff.
7.3 Sustainable Campus Practices

 Maintenance of landscaped green areas across the campus
 Encouragement of eco-friendly practices within academic and administrative units
8. Environmental Awareness Initiatives
Teerthanker Mahaveer University conducts environmental awareness programmes aimed at
promoting responsible environmental practices.
These initiatives may include:
 Cleanliness campaigns and environmental awareness drives

Policy for Persons with Disabilities (PwDs)/Differently Abled Persons
1. Overview
Teerthanker Mahaveer University (TMU) is committed to provide an inclusive and accessible
support to the persons with disabilities/differently abled persons and affirms its responsibility
to remove physical, academic, administrative, and attitudinal barriers that may hinder full
participation of differently abled persons in the University life.
2. Purpose of the Policy
The purpose of this policy is to:
 Ensure equal opportunities for persons with disabilities in education, employment, and
participation
 Promote dignity, independence, and inclusion
 Provide reasonable accommodations and support services
 Align institutional practices with applicable laws and regulations
3. Scope and Applicability
This policy applies to:
 Students with disabilities
 Teaching and non-teaching staff with disabilities
 Visitors and stakeholders with disabilities accessing the campus
 All academic, administrative, residential, and support facilities of TMU
4. Definition
A person with disability refers to an individual with long-term physical, mental, intellectual,
or sensory impairment which, in interaction with barriers, may hinder full and effective
participation in society on an equal basis with others, as defined under applicable laws.
Page 2 of 3
5. Guiding Principles
TMU shall be guided by the following principles:
 Equity and non-discrimination
 Accessibility and universal design
 Respect for dignity
 Participation and inclusion
 Confidentiality and sensitivity
6. Academic Inclusion Measures
The University shall, wherever feasible:
 Provide reasonable academic accommodations such as extra time, assistive devices,
Exam Writing Support or Alternate Assessment Methods etc.
 Facilitate access to learning materials in accessible formats
 Encourage inclusive teaching and evaluation practices
 Support mentoring and academic guidance for students with disabilities
7. Infrastructure and Accessibility
TMU shall progressively work towards:
 Barrier-free access to buildings, classrooms, laboratories, libraries, hostels, and
washrooms
 Inclusive and accessible campus environment by providing infrastructure such as
ramps, lifts, handrails, tactile pathways, and appropriate signage to support differently
abled person.
 Accessible digital platforms and information systems, where applicable
8. Employment and Workplace Inclusion
The University shall:
 Ensure non-discrimination in recruitment, promotion, and service conditions
 Provide reasonable workplace accommodations for employees with disabilities
 Encourage a supportive and inclusive work culture
 Address grievances related to discrimination or accessibility through appropriate
mechanisms

Sustainable Investment Policy
1. Overview
Teerthanker Mahaveer University (TMU) recognizes that investment decisions play a critical
role in supporting long-term institutional sustainability, financial resilience, and responsible
governance. This Sustainable Investment Policy establishes a framework to integrate
environmental, social, and governance (ESG) considerations into investment-related decisions
while ensuring compliance with statutory requirements and fiduciary responsibilities.
This policy supports TMU’s commitment to ethical financial management, responsible
institutional growth, and long-term sustainability, in alignment with globally accepted
principles of good governance and responsible finance.
2. Scope and Applicability
This policy applies to:
 All investment-related decisions undertaken by TMU
 Deployment of funds through endowments, reserves, fixed deposits, instruments, and
other permissible financial avenues
 Decisions taken by statutory committees, finance authorities, or designated officials
responsible for investment management
The policy shall operate in conjunction with applicable financial regulations, University
statutes, and government guidelines.
3. Definition
Sustainable investment refers to an approach to investment decision-making that considers
long-term financial returns while incorporating environmental, social, and governance
considerations, consistent with institutional values, regulatory compliance, and risk
management practices.
Page 2 of 3
4. Objectives
The objectives of this policy are to:
 Ensure responsible and prudent management of University funds
 Integrate sustainability and ethical considerations into investment decisions
 Strengthen long-term financial stability and institutional resilience
 Align investment practices with governance and accountability standards
 Support transparency and risk-aware financial decision-making
5. Guiding Principles
Investment decisions at TMU shall be guided by the following principles:
 Financial prudence: Priority to capital protection and risk management
 Long-term perspective: Consideration of sustainable and stable returns
 Governance and compliance: Adherence to statutory, regulatory, and institutional
norms
 Ethical consideration: Avoidance of investments conflicting with institutional values
 Transparency: Clear documentation and approval processes
6. Sustainable Investment Practices
Wherever applicable and permissible under prevailing regulations, TMU shall:
 Consider ESG-related risks and factors in investment evaluation
 Prefer regulated, transparent, and compliant financial institutions and instruments
 Avoid investment avenues associated with significant regulatory, legal, or ethical
concerns
 Ensure alignment of investment decisions with the University’s long-term objectives
7. Governance and Decision-Making Structure
 Investment decisions shall be undertaken as per University statutes.
 The Governing Body shall ensure that the Planning Board evaluates and prioritizes
investments in green infrastructure, energy efficiency, and environmentally responsible
initiatives while making key financial and developmental decisions.
 All investments shall be subject to approval by the competent authority in accordance
with financial rules of TMU.

Sustainable Procurement / Purchasing Policy
1. Overview
Teerthanker Mahaveer University (TMU) acknowledges that procurement decisions
significantly influence environmental sustainability, social responsibility, financial efficiency,
and institutional governance. This policy establishes a structured framework to ensure that
procurement and purchasing activities are conducted responsibly, ethically, and efficiently
while supporting the University’s long-term sustainability objectives.
2. Scope and Applicability
This policy applies to:
 All academic, administrative, clinical, residential, and support units of TMU
 Procurement of goods, services, works, utilities, and outsourced activities
 All procurement modes including tenders, quotations, rate contracts, and service
agreements
The policy applies to all officials involved in procurement planning, approval, execution, and
monitoring.
3. Definition
Sustainable procurement refers to the acquisition of goods, services, and works in a manner
that achieves value for money across the full life cycle, while giving due consideration to
environmental protection, social responsibility, ethical conduct, and economic efficiency.
4. Objectives
The objectives of this policy are to:
 Promote responsible and efficient use of institutional resources
 Integrate sustainability considerations into procurement decisions where feasible
 Encourage ethical and compliant supplier practices
Page 2 of 3
 Minimize environmental impact associated with procurement activities
 Ensure compliance with statutory, regulatory, and institutional requirements
 Strengthen transparency and accountability in procurement processes
5. Guiding Principles
Procurement at TMU shall be guided by:
 Need-based purchasing to avoid wasteful expenditure
 Life-cycle perspective considering durability, maintenance, and disposal
 Environmental responsibility wherever applicable
 Social and ethical responsibility in supplier engagement
 Transparency, fairness, and competitiveness in procurement processes
6. Responsible Procurement Practices
Wherever feasible and appropriate, TMU shall:
 Encourage sourcing from compliant and responsible suppliers
 Prefer products and services that are energy-efficient, reusable, or recyclable
 Promote efficient use of materials and reduction of waste
 Discourage procurement from suppliers with a history of statutory or regulatory non-
compliance
 Include sustainability-related considerations in procurement documentation, where
relevant
7. Supplier Responsibilities
Suppliers and service providers are expected to:
 Comply with applicable environmental, labour, health, and safety regulations
 Adhere to ethical business practices
 Avoid use of prohibited or environmentally hazardous materials
 Cooperate with institutional requirements related to responsible procurement
8. Governance and Implementation
 The Purchase Committee / Central Purchase Department shall oversee implementation
 Procurement decisions shall align with existing financial rules and procedures

Anti-Bribery and Corruption Policy
1. Purpose
Teerthanker Mahaveer University (TMU) is committed to the highest standards of
integrity, ethical conduct, transparency, fairness, and accountability in all academic,
administrative, and business activities. This Anti-Bribery and Corruption Policy set out
TMU’s zero-tolerance approach to bribery and corruption and supports compliance
with applicable Indian anti-corruption laws, including the Prevention of Corruption Act,
1988, and related regulations.
2. Scope
This Policy applies to all University stakeholders, including but not limited to:
 University Governing & Statutory Bodies, Officers, Administrators, Faculty, Staff, and
Students;
 Consultants, contractors, agents, vendors, suppliers, and third-party representatives;
 Collaborators, partners, and any individual or entity acting on behalf of TMU.
3. Definitions
Bribery – Offering, promising, giving, receiving or soliciting, directly or indirectly,
any item of value (monetary or otherwise) to improperly influence a decision or secure
an unfair advantage.
Corruption – Abuse of entrusted power for personal gain, including bribery,
favouritism, nepotism, embezzlement, or other unethical conduct.
Facilitation Payments – Small unofficial payments made to expedite administrative
actions; these are strictly prohibited.
Conflict of Interest – A situation where personal, financial, or other interests could
compromise or appear to compromise objective decision-making.
Page 2 of 3
4. Policy Statement
TMU adopts a strict zero-tolerance position regarding bribery and corruption. All forms of
bribery and corrupt practices are prohibited in all University operations, whether on-campus,
off-campus, or digital:
 Offering, promising, giving, soliciting, or receiving bribes or undue advantages;
 Influence or attempt to influence University decisions (e.g., admissions, examinations,
recruitment, procurement, research funding) through illicit inducements;
 Improper use of University resources for personal benefit;
 Collusive practices to distort fair outcomes.
5. Gifts, Hospitality, and Entertainment
Gifts, hospitality and entertainment that could reasonably create an appearance of impropriety
are prohibited, however reasonable tokens of appreciation may be acceptable if:
 They are modest, customary, and not intended to influence a decision; and
 Prior approval is obtained from the relevant authority when the value exceeds defined
University thresholds.
6. Due Diligence and Controls
TMU shall:
 Undertake due diligence when engaging third-party partners, contractors, and vendors;
 Maintain robust internal controls, financial transparency, and documentation of
transactions;
 Conduct regular risk assessments to identify potential vulnerabilities.
7. Reporting Mechanisms
All stakeholders are encouraged and obligated to report any suspicion or knowledge of bribery
or corruption, including through confidential and protected channels such as:
 Dedicated reporting email or portal;
 Compliance Office or Code of Conduct Committee.
TMU will take all reports seriously, investigate impartially, and protect whistleblowers
from retaliation.

ANTI-HARASSMENT POLICY
1. Introduction:
Teerthanker Mahaveer University (TMU), recognizes the value of a safe, inclusive, respectful,
and equitable academic and workplace environment. The University adopts a zero-tolerance
approach toward harassment in any form, including verbal, physical, psychological, sexual, or
digital misconduct. This policy outlines TMU’s strong commitment to maintaining a
harassment-free environment across the campus and beyond in alignment with the
Prevention of Sexual Harassment Act 2013 (POSH Act 2013).
2. Purpose:
It aims to:
 Prevent all forms of harassment and discrimination
 Promote a culture of dignity, respect, and inclusion
 Provide a structured mechanism for reporting, redressal, and resolution
 Ensure compliance with statutory provisions (POSH Act 2013, etc.)
 Strengthen institutional accountability and transparency
3. Scope and Applicability
This policy applies to all:
 Faculties, departments, and administrative units

 Visitors, vendors, consultants, and third-party stakeholders
 All university premises, hostels, transport, events, and digital platforms
Page 2 of 5
4. DeﬁniƟons
Harassment
Any unwelcome behaviour (verbal, non-verbal, physical, or digital) that creates an
intimidating, hostile, or offensive environment.
Sexual Harassment
Includes but is not limited to:
 Unwelcome physical contact or advances
 Demand/request for sexual favours
 Display of inappropriate content
Workplace Harassment
Bullying, intimidation, humiliation, or discrimination affecting professional or academic
performance.
Cyber Harassment
Harassment through emails, social media, messaging platforms, or other digital means.

Sustainability and Climate AcƟon Policy
1.Introduction:
Teerthanker Mahaveer University (TMU) recognizes the importance of environmental sustainability
and responsible resource management as an integral part of its institutional values. The University
promotes practices that conserve natural resources, reduce environmental impact, and support
climate-responsive operations across campus activities and functions. This policy outlines TMU’s
commitment to sustainability and climate action in alignment with its institutional values and
ongoing environmental initiatives.
2. Purpose:
The purpose of this policy is to provide a clear framework for guiding sustainable practices and
climate action across academic, administrative, and operational domains at TMU. It aims to:
 Encourage eco-friendly resource use and responsible campus behaviour
 Establish principles for sustainable infrastructure and energy use
 Support water conservation and waste management systems
 Strengthen monitoring and review of environmental performance
3. Scope and Applicability
This policy applies to all:
 Faculties, departments, and administrative units
 Students, faculty, and staff
 Campus infrastructure, facilities, and services
 Operations involving energy use, water use, transportation, and waste management
Page 2 of 3
4. DeﬁniƟons
Sustainability
Using resources in ways that do not compromise the ability of future generations to meet their own
needs.
Climate Action
Actions that reduce an organization’s carbon footprint, improve resource efficiency, and mitigate
environmental risks.
5. Guiding Principles
TMU shall be guided by the following principles:
 Resource Efficiency: Reduce energy and water consumption while promoting renewable
and efficient technologies.
 Preventive Environmental Management: Reduce pollution, enforce waste management,
and discourage harmful practices (e.g., single-use plastics).
 Campus Inclusivity and Awareness: Encourage participation and awareness among all
campus stakeholders.
 Compliance and Responsibility: Follow applicable statutory and environmental standards.

 TMU operates a 1345kWp rooftop solar (PV) power plant which generates 4,500 units per
day.
6.2 Green Campus IniƟaƟves
 Restrict vehicular entry to designated areas; promote access for resident and service
vehicles only
 Encourage use of bicycles and battery-operated vehicles for campus mobility
 Provide well-planned pedestrian pathways to reduce reliance on motor vehicles
 Prohibit single-use plastic across campus and support Swachhta (cleanliness) campaigns

Equity, Diversity and Inclusion (EDI) Policy
1. Introduction:
Teerthanker Mahaveer University (TMU) recognizes the importance of equity, diversity, and
aspects of inclusion as an integral part of its core institutional ethics and values. The University
promotes various direct and indirect practices that are aligned with the notion of Equity,
Diversity, and Inclusion (EDI). It reflects in various operations across campus activities and
functions. This policy outlines TMU’s commitment to Equity, Diversity, and Inclusion in
alignment with its institutional values and ongoing initiatives.
2. Purpose:
The purpose of this policy is to provide a clear framework for EDI practices and their impact
across academic, administrative, society, and operational domains at TMU. It aims to:
 PromoƟng equity of opportunity
 Nurture a culture of inclusion and belonging
 EliminaƟng discriminaƟon, harassment, and vicƟmizaƟon
 Valuing diversity as a strength that enhances academic and social outcomes
3. Scope and Applicability
This policy applies to all:
 Colleges, departments, and administrative units
 Students, faculty, and staff
 Contractors, consultants, and visitors
 InsƟtuƟonal partners and collaborators
Page 2 of 4
4. DeﬁniƟons
Equity
Ensure fair treatment, access, and opportuniƟes for all individuals, removing barriers that may
disadvantage any group.
Diversity
Recognize, respect, and celebrate diﬀerences, including but not limited to:
 Gender and gender idenƟty
 Age
 Disability
 Socio-economic background
 Religion and belief
 Ethnicity and culture
Inclusion
Create an environment where everyone feels valued, heard, and empowered to par Ɵcipate
fully.
5. Guiding Principles
TMU shall be guided by the following principles:
 Equity of opportunity: ensuring fair access to educa Ɵon, employment, par ƟcipaƟon,
and advancement.
 Dignity and respect: fostering a campus culture that values every person and rejects
prejudice.
 Inclusion and belonging: creaƟng condi Ɵons in which individuals from diverse
backgrounds can parƟcipate fully and conﬁdently.
 Accessibility: removing physical, digital, communica Ɵon, and procedural barriers for
persons with disabiliƟes and others facing disadvantage.
 RepresentaƟon: encouraging balanced parƟcipaƟon in student enrolment, staﬃng, and
leadership.
 Accountability: assigning responsibility for implementa Ɵon, review , and correc Ɵve
acƟon.
 Evidence-based improvement: using data, feedback, and periodic review to strengthen
outcomes over Ɵme.
Page 3 of 4
6. ImplementaƟon Framework
6.1 Leadership and Governance
 Establish an EDI CommiƩee responsible for oversight and policy implementaƟon
 Integrate EDI metrics into insƟtuƟonal performance indicators
6.2 Recruitment and Employment PracƟces
 Ensure fair, transparent, and inclusive recruitment processes
 Conduct regular reviews of hiring, promoƟon, and compensaƟon pracƟces
 Provide equal opportuniƟes for training, development, and career progression
6.3 Training and Capacity Building
 EDI awareness and sensiƟvity training for all staﬀ
 Leadership training on inclusive pracƟces and unconscious bias
 Student orientaƟon programs promoƟng respect and diversity
6.4 Inclusive Learning Environment
 Design curricula that reﬂect diverse perspecƟves
 Ensure accessibility in physical and digital infrastructure
 Provide support services for underrepresented and disadvantaged groups
7. Roles and ResponsibiliƟes
7.1 Governing Body / ExecuƟve Leadership
The governing authority and execuƟve leadership shall provide visible commitment, approve
policy direcƟon, ensure resourcing, and review insƟtuƟonal progress on Equity and inclusion.
7.2 Vice Chancellor
The Vice Chancellor shall provide strategic leadership for implementaƟon, accountability, and
annual review of EDI performance indicators.
7.3 EDI CommiƩee
A designated Equity, Diversity and Inclusion CommiƩee shall:
 Oversee implementaƟon of this policy.

HOSTEL STRUCTURE
OBJECTIVE
Hostel is like a home for the students in campus. Accordingly the students should be facilitated by the
all utility services facilities, food essential commodities, sports and events and hygienic environment
for residing in the hostel. As well as students should be in a manner that’s bring credit to him/her and
to the university.
INFRASTUCTURE
There are separate hostels in the university campus
A. Girls hostel
B. Boys hostel
Girls hostel have three independent blocks as under
I. New Girls Hostel
II. MBBS Girls Hostel
III. Girls Hostel Block A
Boys hostel have three independent blocks as under
I. Boys Hostel Block B
II. Old Boys Hostel
III. New Boys Hostel

FACILITIES
1. A hygienic mess provided in each block of the boys and girls hostels.
2. Canteen facility is available for 24*7.
3. In case of illness of the student, food is provided as per the instruction of medical advice but no
case any non-vegetarian food is allowed in the hostels.
4. Proper housekeeping staff is assigned for the maintenance of the cleaning in hostel premises and
each room.
5. Computer lab is provided in each hostel with LAN connection.
6. Gym facility is available for the hostellers.
7. News papers are available in the each block of the hostels.
8. Laundry & washer man service are available in the each block of the hostel at door delivery.
9. Common room / T.V room with indoor games are available in the each blocks of the hostel.
10. Although very good indoor stadium and outdoor game fa cilities are available in the campus.
Some sports facilities e.g. basket ball, badminton is provided in the hostel premises.
11. RO system duly fitted with water cooler is available in each block of the hostel for the water
purification.
12. Wi-Fi facilities are available in each block of the hostels.
13. All required furniture and fixtures are available with each room of the hostel.
14. Electricity and water supply is available round the clock except maintenance.
15. CCTV Cameras are fitted in all important areas of each blo ck in the hostels for the security
purpose.
16. A 1000 bedded hospital is available in the premises for the medical facilities to the hostellers.
17. A hot water facility is available in each block.
18. Visitor Room is available in each block of hostels for the parents and relative of the students.
19. Yoga and meditation facilities are available.
20. Study rooms are available in the hostels.
REPORTING SYSTEM
1. After taking admission student report to Chief Warden Office / Admission cell for taking hostel
facility.
2. Student fil l “HOSTEL ALLOTMENT FORM” with hostel management system software received
from Chief Warden Office/ Admission cell and then submit the fees at the cash counter.
3. Student show the fees receipt in Chief Warden Office/ Admission Cell. Hostel facilities are allowed
only after submission of all prescribed hostel charges.
4. Room is allotted to the student as per their respected course and category chosen with the
availability in respected hostel by the Warden Office.
GENERAL HOSTEL RULES & REGULATIONS
Hostel rules are available in the “Student’s Diary” for hostellers as Annexure -1.
7 | P a g e
STUDENTS’ GRIEVANCE REDRESSAL SYSTEM/
DESCIPILNARY ACTION
In order to promote a responsive and conducive environment into the hostel a ‘Students’ Grievance
Redressal Cell’ is established. The ‘Cell’ shall provide a friendly mechanism to the students to report
their grievances and the faster disposal of the same. It shall also provide a platform to the students to
come forward with constructive suggestions for more efficient and effective atmosphere. [NOTE: The
term “Grievance” refers to a difficulty, problem, or a feeling of discontent at individual student level
due to an act/omission of the staff of the hostel]
HOSTEL ANTI RAGGING/GRIVENCES COMMITTEE
PROCEDURE TO FILE A GRIEVANCE/SUGGESTION
A student may approach the Students’ Grievance Redressal Cell in person and file her/his
grievance/suggestion in the prescribed format. A student may also drop the completed Performa in
the Suggestion/ Grievance Box placed in front of each mess of the hostels.
No student is allowed to file a grievance/suggestion on behalf of any other student.
GRIEVANCE PROCESSING
Grievance committee is providing a free and fair environment to students so that they can express
their difficulties/problems without any apprehension.
It ensures early and effective solution to a student’s problem and provide/suggest ways and means so
that such an issue does not arise in future.
Counseling of the students is to be maintaining dignity and decorum, and to exercise restraint and
patience as per demand of the situation in the hostel.
Ensuring friendly environment in the hostel will be by promoting cordial Student -Student and
Student-Staff relations.
GRIEVANCES RELATED TO MAINTENANCE
1. Students note down their complaint in complaint register placed in warden office.
2. Maintenance department fulfill the complaint as soon as possible.
