Circular
Sub: Regarding the Re-constitution of the Students’ Grievance Redressal Committee
(earlier University Grievance Redressal Committee).
In accordance with the provisions of the UGC (Redressal of Grievances of Students)
Regulations, 2023, the University has re-constituted the Students’ Grievance Redressal
Committee (earlier University Grievance Redressal Committee).
Composition of Students’ Grievance Redressal Committee (SGRC)
1. A Professor Chairperson
2. Four Professors/Senior Faculty Members of the Institution Member
3. A representative from among students to be nominated on academic
merit/excellence in sports/performance in co-curricular activities
Special Invitee
* At least one member or the Chairperson shall be a woman and at least one member or the
Chairperson shall be from SC/ST/OBC category.
*The term of the Chairperson and members shall be for a period of two years.
*The term of the special invitee shall be one year.
*The quorum for the meeting including the Chairperson, but excluding the special invitee, shall
be three.
Students’ Grievance Redressal Committee
In case of grievances not resolved by Department/College Grievance Redressal C ell
(DGRC/CGRC), it shall be referred to the Students’ Grievance Redressal Committee which is
constituted as below:
1 Prof. Vipin Jain, Principal, TMIMT College of Management Chairperson
2 Prof. M.P. Singh, Dean Students’ Welfare Member
3 Dr. Sudhir Singh, Professor Microbiology, TM Medical College &
Research Centre
Member
4 Prof. Ankita Jain, Vice- Principal, TM Dental College & Research
Centre
Member
5 Head of the Department/Principal of the College - Chairperson of the
DGRC/CGRC
Member
6 A representative from among students to be nominated on academic
merit/excellence in sports/performance in co-curricular activities-
from Concerned DGRC/CGRC
Special Invitee
The SGRC shall send its report with recommendations, if any, to the competent authority of the
University and a copy thereof to the aggrieved student, preferably within a period of 15 working
days from the date of receipt of the complaint.
Any student aggrieved by the decision of the Students’ Grievance Redressal Committee may
prefer an appeal to the Ombudsperson, within a period of fifteen days from the date of receipt of
such decision.
Composition of Department/College Grievance Redressal Cell:
1 A Professor (Head of the Department/Principal of the
College)
Chairperson
2 A Professor from outside the Department/College to be
nominated by the Vice Chancellor
Member
3 A representative from among students to be nominated
on academic merit/excellence in sports/performance in
co-curricular activities
Special Invitee
4 A faculty member well-versed with grievance
redressal mechanism to be nominated by the Principal
of the College
Member Secretary
Functions of Cell/ Committee:
To address the grievances of the students related with:
i. Admission contrary to merit determined in accordance with the declared admission policy of
the institution;
ii. Irregularity in the process under the declared admission policy of the institution;
iii. Refusal to admit in accordance with the declared admission policy of the institution;
iv. Non-publication of a prospectus by the institution, in accordance with the provisions of
these regulations;
v. Publication by the institution of any information in the prospectus, which is false or
misleading, and not based on facts;
vi. Withholding of, or refusal to return, any document in the form of certificates of degree,
diploma or any other award or other document deposited by a student for the purpose of
seeking admission in such institution, with a view to induce or compel such student to pay
any fee or fees in respect of any course or program of study which such student does not
intend to pursue;
vii. Demand of money in excess of that specified to be charged in the declared admission policy
of the institution;
viii. Violation, by the institution, of any law for the time being in force in regard to reservation of
seats in admission to different category of students;
ix. Non-payment or delay in payment of scholarships or financial aid admissible to any student
under the declared admission policy of such institution, or under the conditions, if any,
prescribed by the Commission;
x. Delay by the institution in the conduct of examinations, or declaration of results, beyond the
schedule specified in the academic calendar of the institution, or in such calendar prescribed
by the Commission;
xi. Failure by the institution to provide student amenities as set out in the prospectus, or is
required to be extended by the institution under any provisions of law for the time being in
force;
xii. Non-transparent or unfair practices adopted by the institution for the evaluation of students;
xiii. Delay in, or denial of, the refund of fees due to a student who withdraws admission within
the time mentioned in the prospectus, subject to guidelines, if any, issued by the
Commission, from time to time;
xiv. Complaints of alleged discrimination of students from the Scheduled Castes, the Scheduled
Tribes, Other Backward Classes, Women, Minorities or persons with disabilities categories;
xv. Denial of quality education as promised at the time of admission or required to be provided;
xvi. Harassment or victimization of a student, other than cases of harassment, which are to be
proceeded against under the penal provisions of any law for the time being in force;
xvii. Any action initiated/taken contrary to the statutes, ordinances, rules, regulations, or
guidelines of the institution; and
xviii. Any action initiated/taken contrary to the regulations and/or guidelines made/issued by the
Commission and/or the regulatory body concerned.
The DGRC/CGRC shall send its report with recommendations, if any, to the SGRC and a copy
thereof to the aggrieved student, preferably within a period of 15 working days from the date of
receipt of the complaint.
The College Principals/HoDs are requested to form the cell of their College/Department
and send the same in the Registrar office for further approval of Hon’ble Vice Chancellor
latest by 23.09.2024.
This is issued with the approval of Hon’ble Vice Chancellor.
Dr. Aditya Sharma
(Registrar)

Eligibility Criteria of MeritProgramme & Specializations
At Teerthanker Mahaveer University, we believe that the meritorious
students should be rewarded and should not be left out of the main
stream in their quest for higher education. Scholarships at the
university are provided to outstanding students. Thus, to recognize
the talent of meritorious and needy students, the university has
provision of scholarships, medals, awards and certiﬁcates.
Regulations governing these scholarships/awards can be amended
from time to time as per the discretion of the University.
SCHOLARSHIP SCHEME
Scholarship for Jain Students:
• All Jain students will be given upto 50% exemption in Tuition fees
and upto 30% in hostel fees for the entire duration of the
programme. No scholarship in D.El.Ed. (BTC), Dental and
Medical.*
• Multiple scholarships will not be available.
Enrollment Fee Rs. 1,000/- (One Time) for all programmes except Medical, All Diploma programmes of Nursing ,
Paramedical & Physiotherapy, BTC and Rs. 1,000/- for B.A. & M.A. in Jainology
Admission Registration Fee Rs. 5,000/- (One Time) for all programmes except Medical & Dental.
Admission Processing Fee Rs. 2,500/- (One Time) for all programmes except Medical & Dental.
Lab Charges Rs. 500/- per semester for all semester programmes & Rs. 1,000/- per year for all annual
programmes.
University Uniform Cloth Material Free
Other Fee Each student in the final year of the programmes shall be required to pay a nominal amount of Rs.
2,500/- towards the Convocation charges and Rs. 500/- towards Alumni charges along with the final
year fee.

1. The University
The Annual Report for the Academic Session 2023–24 of the University attempts to reflect the
various facets of the University and its constituent colleges. As expected of an academic
institution, Teerthanker Mahaveer University has grown steadily in terms of infrastructure and
the addition of contemporary courses with a dynamic curriculum.
Teerthanker Mahaveer University is a Jain Minority State Private University established by Act
No. 30 of 2008 of the Government of Uttar Pradesh, and is approved by the University Grants
Commission (UGC) under Section 2(f) and the UGC (Establishment of and Maintenance of
Standards in Private Universities) Regulations, 2003. The University is located on National
Highway-09 and is just 144 km from the National Capital, New Delhi. The University remains
committed to the ideals of Lord Mahaveer—Right Philosophy, Right Knowledge, and Right
Conduct—in all its operations and aspires to be recognized as a premier institution in India
and abroad.
The University owes its origin to Teerthanker Mahaveer Institute of Management and
Technology (TMIMT), which forayed into professional education in 2001 by offering courses
such as BBA, BCA, MCA, MBA, and B.Ed. After the University came into existence in 2008, these
programs have been offered under the TMIMT College of Management, the College of
Computing Sciences & Information Technology, and the College of Education. Subsequently,
colleges and departments such as Dental, Medical, Engineering, Pharmacy, Nursing,
Paramedical Sciences, Physiotherapy, Law, Physical Education, Polytechnic, Fine Arts, Jain
Studies, and Agricultural Sciences were established to meet the rising aspirations of the youth.
Currently, the University offers a wide range of programs with high employability potential
through its 14 on-campus colleges and 2 independent departments. The University has
established extensive collaborative arrangements with leading national and international
institutions to ensure quality education.
The existence of any university lies in the creation of new knowledge through research aimed
at improving the lives of people. To strengthen research in the larger interest of society and
to provide a platform for its faculty and researchers to share their experiences and innovations
with the world, the University publishes six in-house research journals, namely: Viewpoint in
Management, S&T Review in Engineering, Pharmacoarena in Pharmacy, TMU Journal of
Dentistry in Dental Sciences, Acta Medica International in Medical Sciences, and IJRTCSIT in
Computer Science disciplines.
The University stands as a beacon of excellence in education, with a distinguished array of
achievements and accolades. It proudly holds UGC 12B status, signifying its recognized
standing in higher education. Its Innovation and Incubation Centre (IIC) has earned a
Page 2 of 137
prestigious 4-Star Rating, endorsed by rigorous standards of innovation. Recognized by the
Government of Uttar Pradesh under its start-up policy, the University’s Business Incubation
Centre, established in 2018, fosters cutting -edge entrepreneurial ventures. The NBA
accreditation of its B.Tech. (CSE) program underscores its commitment to quality technical
education. With NAAC Accreditation Grade-A and a commendable overall score of 3.15, the
University ensures high standards across all disciplines. DSIR registration further enhances its
credibility as a hub for scientific research and development. The ICAR accreditation of its B.Sc.
(Hons.) Agriculture program reflects its leadership in agricultural education and research.
NABH accreditation of the University Hospital reinforces its commitment to healthcare
excellence. Recognized as a SIRO by the Government, the University facilitates significant
research partnerships. ISO certification and NABL accreditation further validate its operational
and academic standards. An ‘A’ Grade by QCI for its Nursing and Paramedical disciplines
highlights its excellence in healthcare education. As a proud member of UNAI (United Nations
Academic Impact), the University is globally connected in advancing educational goals.
Recently awarded Diamond Band status as an Institution of Prominence in the OBE Rankings
2024 and positioned in the prestigious 51–100 band in the Innovation category of the NIRF
India Rankings 2023, it continues to lead through innovation and academic distinction.
Achieving Diamond Category status in the Sustainable Institutions of India Green Rankings
2024 further underscores the University’s commitment to sustainability. Securing Rank 11
among India’s Top Private Universities for Medicine and Allied Courses, and Rank 4 in Uttar
Pradesh for Teerthanker Mahaveer College of Pharmacy by IIRF, stands as a testament to its
exceptional contributions to healthcare education and research.
Teerthanker Mahaveer University Campus

About the founders
Chancellor Shri. Suresh Jain, along with Group Vice Chairman Shri. Manish Jain, initiated the
mammoth task of establishing a world-class university. The duo has been incessantly
engaged in strategic planning to create an environment that offers not only quality education
but also value-added courses, along with excellent communication and skill development, to
enhance employment and entrepreneurship opportunities—enabling students to find a
meaningful place in society.

3. University Vision & Mission
Vision
To be internationally recognized as a premier institution of excellence providing
quality education, research and consultancy services to the society.
Mission
Our endeavor is to impart knowledge and develop critical skills necessary to
succeed both in professional and personal life by promoting learning, supported by
world-class faculty, infrastructure, technology, curricula, collaborative teaching and
research with premier institutions in India and abroad.

P a g e 2 | 269
1 The University
The Annual Repo rt for the academic session 2022 -23 of the University attempts to reflect the
various facets of the University and its colleges. As is expected of an academic institution,
Teerthanker Mahaveer University has grown steadily in terms of its infrastructure and addition of
contemporary courses with a dynamic curriculum.
Teerthanker Mahaveer University is a Jain Minority State Private University established by Act No.
30 of 2008 of the Government of Uttar Pradesh and has been approved by University Grants
Commission (UGC) under Section 2(f) and UGC (Establishment of and Maintenance of Standards in
Private University) Regulations, 2003. The university is located on Old National Highway -24 and is
barely 144 Kms from National Capital, New Delhi. The University stands committed to the ideals of
Lord Mahaveer i.e. Right Philosophy, Right Knowledge, and Right Conduct in all its operations and
aspire to be recognized as premier institutions in India and abroad.
The University owes its origin to Teerthanker Mahaveer Institute of Management and Technolog y
(TMIMT), which forayed into professional education in the year 2001 by offering courses such as
BBA, BCA, MCA, MBA and B.Ed. After the university came into existence in 2008, these programs
are being run under the TMIMT College of Management, College of Computing Sciences &
Information Technology and College of Education. Subsequently, colleges/departments like: Dental,
Medical, Engineering, Pharmacy, Nursing, Para -medical Sciences, Physiothe rapy, Law, Physical
Education, Polytechnic, Fine Arts, Jain Stud ies and Agriculture Sciences have b een created to meet
the rising aspirations of the youth. Currently, the University offers wide range of programs having
high employability potential through its 14 on -campus colleges and 2 independent departments.
The Uni versity has made extensive collaborative arrangements with leading national and
international institutions to ensure quality education.
The existence of any university lies in the creation of new knowledge through research in order to
improve the lives of people. For strengthening the research in the larger interest of the society and
to provide a platform to its faculty and researchers to share their research experience and
innovations with the world, the University is publishing six in -house research jou rnals viz.
Viewpoint in Management, S&T Review in Engineering, Pharmacoarena in Pharmacy, TMU Journal
of Dentistry in Dental Sciences, Acta Medica International in the Medical Sciences, and IJRTCSIT in
Computer Science disciplines.
The university stands as a beacon of excellence in education with a distinguished array of
achievements and accolades. It proudly holds UGC 12B status, signifying its recognized status in
higher education. Its Innovation and Incubation Centre (IIC) has ear ned a prestigious 4 Star Rating,
endorsed by rigorous standards of innovation. Recognized by the Government of Uttar Pradesh
under its start -up policy, its Business Incubation Centre, established in 2018, fosters cutting -edge
entrepreneurial ventures. The NBA accreditation of its B. Tech. (CSE) program underscores its
commitment to quality technical education. With NAAC Accreditation Grade -A and a commendable
overall score of 3.15, the university ensures high standards across all disciplines. DSIR registrat ion
further enhances its credibility as a hub for scientific research and development. The ICAR
accreditation of its B. Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture program reflects its leadership in agricultural
education and research. Recognized as a SIRO by the government, it facilitates significant research
P a g e 3 | 269
partnerships. ISO certification and NABL Certification further validate its operational and academic
standards. As a proud member of UNAI (United Nations Academic Impact), the university is globally
connected in advancin g educational goals. Awarded Gold band status as an Institution of
Prominence in OBE Rankings 2023, and positioned in the prestigious band of 51 -100 in the
Innovation category of NIRF India rankings 2023, it continues to lead through innovation and
academic distinction. Achieving Grade A with Gold Category in Sustainable Institutions of India
Green Rankings 2023 further underscores its commitment to sustainability. Rank 11 among India’s
Top Private Universities for Medicine and Allied Courses and Teerthanke r Mahaveer College of
Pharmacy securing Rank 4 in Uttar Pradesh by IIRF are testament to its exceptional contributions to
the field of healthcare education and research.
Teerthanker Mahaveer University Campus
About the founders
Chancellor Shri Suresh Jain along with Group Vice Chairman Shri Manish Jain initiated the
mammoth job of setting up of a world class University and the duo is incessantly engaged in the
strategic planning to create an environment for providing not only quality education b ut also
value added courses along with excellent communication and skills for better employment and
entrepreneurship avenues enabling its students to find a meaningful place in the society.

3 University Vision & Mission
Vision
To be internationally recognized as a premier
institution of excellence providing quality
education, research and consultancy services
to the society.
Mission
Our endeavor is to impart knowledge and develop critical skills necessary to
succeed both in professional and personal life by promoting learning, supported
by world-class faculty, infrastructure, technology, curricula, collaborative
teaching and research with premier institutions in India and abroad.

4 Why TMU
1. UGC approved more than 150 programmes across 14 on- campus colleges and an
independent department.
